recommended.name: Talar Tilt Test
recommended.procedure: The ankle is held in the neutral position, examiner stabilises the tibia just above the ankle and then tries to force the ankle into maximum inversion. The ROM can be measured or compared with the contralateral side. Inversion laxity suggests injury to calcaneofibular and anterior talofibular ligaments (ATFL).

recommended.name: Anterior Drawer Test
recommended.procedure: Patient sits with knee flexed at 90 deg and ankle in plantarflexion of about 10 deg. The lower leg is stabilised by the examiner and forces patient's heel forward over the tibia. If positive, the talus can be felt sliding forwards and backwards. Laxity indicates tear of the ATFL.

recommended.name: Talar Tilt Test
recommended.procedure: The ankle is held in the neutral position, examiner stabilises the tibia just above the ankle and then tries to force the ankle into maximum inversion. The ROM can be measured or compared with the contralateral side. Inversion laxity suggests injury to calcaneofibular and anterior talofibular ligaments (ATFL).

recommended.name: Anterior Drawer Test
recommended.procedure: Patient sits with knee flexed at 90 deg and ankle in plantarflexion of about 10 deg. The lower leg is stabilised by the examiner and forces patient's heel forward over the tibia. If positive, the talus can be felt sliding forwards and backwards. Laxity indicates tear of the ATFL.

recommended.name: Spurling's Test (Maximal Cervical Compression and Foraminal Compression Test)
recommended.procedure: The neck is placed in extension, lateral flexion, and axial compression. The test is positive if pain is present and radiates to the arm.

recommended.name: Cervical Distraction Test
recommended.procedure: The patient lies supine and the neck is positioned comfortably. The examiner places hand around the patient's mastoid process. The examiner then slightly flexes the patient's neck and pulls the head towards your torso. Test is positive if the symptoms reduce or are eliminated with traction.

questionResponseTests.question: Where is the pain located?

recommended.name: FABER Test (Patrick’s Test)
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Affected leg is placed in flexion, abduction, and external rotation (figure-4). Examiner applies gentle downward pressure on knee while stabilizing opposite ASIS.

recommended.name: FADIR Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes hip to 90°, then adducts and internally rotates hip.

recommended.name: Scour Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes and adducts hip, applies axial compression along femur while sweeping hip in an arc between adduction/internal rotation and abduction/external rotation.

recommended.name: Log Roll Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with legs extended. Examiner gently rolls the entire leg into internal and external rotation.

recommended.name: Trendelenburg Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands unsupported on affected leg for 30 seconds. Examiner observes pelvic tilt.

recommended.name: Resisted Quadriceps Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is seated with knee slightly flexed. Examiner applies resistance as the patient extends the knee.

recommended.name: Step-Down Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands on a 20 cm step and slowly lowers contralateral heel to the ground while examiner observes alignment.

recommended.name: Clarke’s Test (Patellar Grind Test)
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with knee extended. Examiner applies gentle downward pressure on superior pole of patella while patient contracts quadriceps.

recommended.name: Patellar Apprehension Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine and relaxed. Examiner pushes the patella laterally.

recommended.name: Patellar Tilt Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with knee extended. Examiner lifts the lateral edge of the patella.

recommended.name: Waldron Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is seated and actively flexes and extends knee while examiner palpates patellofemoral joint.

recommended.name: Patellar Glide Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with knee extended. Examiner glides patella medially and laterally.

questionResponseTests.question: Do you have recent twisting injury?

recommended.name: McMurray Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes the hip and knee fully, then rotates the tibia internally and externally while extending the knee.

recommended.name: Apley’s Compression Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies prone with knee flexed to 90°. Examiner applies downward axial pressure along tibia while rotating it internally and externally.

recommended.name: Thessaly Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands on one leg with knee flexed to 20°. Patient rotates body and knee internally and externally three times.

recommended.name: Joint Line Tenderness Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates along medial and lateral tibiofemoral joint lines with knee flexed to 90°.

recommended.name: Bounce Home Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner fully flexes the knee and then allows it to passively extend.

recommended.name: Ege’s Test
recommended.procedure: Patient squats with knees flexed and externally rotates feet (medial meniscus) or internally rotates feet (lateral meniscus).

recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine with legs extended. Examiner asks patient to lift affected leg straight up without bending knee.

recommended.name: Patellar Tap / Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine with knee relaxed. Examiner palpates patella gently feeling for gap, step-off, or bone fragment displacement.

recommended.name: Ottawa Knee Rules Assessment
recommended.procedure: Assess age (≥55), isolated patellar tenderness, fibular head tenderness, flexion <90°, or inability to bear weight 4 steps.

recommended.procedure: Palpate medial and lateral tibial condyles and tibial plateau margins.

recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine with knee extended. Examiner palpates anteromedial proximal tibia, 5–7 cm below medial joint line.

recommended.name: Resisted Knee Flexion Test
recommended.procedure: Patient flexes knee from 90° while examiner applies manual resistance.

recommended.name: Resisted Hip Adduction Test
recommended.procedure: Patient performs hip adduction against examiner resistance.

recommended.name: Hamstring Stretch Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner passively extends knee with hip flexed, stretching hamstring tendons.

recommended.name: Joint Line Differentiation Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates medial joint line and pes anserine region sequentially.

recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates medial aspect of popliteal fossa between semimembranosus and medial gastrocnemius head.

recommended.name: Transillumination Test
recommended.procedure: Light source placed against posterior knee swelling in a dimmed examination room.

recommended.name: Knee Effusion Stroke Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner performs sweep/stroke test across medial and lateral parapatellar gutters.

recommended.name: Passive Joint Motion Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner gently moves patient’s knee through minimal passive flexion and extension.

recommended.name: Local Temperature Assessment
recommended.procedure: Examiner uses dorsum of hand to compare skin temperature of affected knee to contralateral knee.

recommended.name: Joint Effusion Test (Bulge / Ballottement Test)
recommended.procedure: Examiner applies downward pressure on suprapatellar pouch and ballottes patella against femur.

recommended.name: Diagnostic Arthrocentesis (Gold Standard)
recommended.procedure: Sterile needle joint aspiration for synovial fluid WBC count, Gram stain, crystals, and culture.

recommended.name: Bicycle Stress Test
recommended.procedure: Record the amount of time the patient spends on a cycle ergometer while in a neutral lumbar position and slumped position. If patient spends more time in the slumped position, a lumbar spinal stenosis is indicated.

recommended.name: Two-stage Treadmill Test
recommended.procedure: The patient walks on a flat treadmill and the amount of time spent is recorded and compared with the amount of time while the treadmill is inclined such that patient walks in flexion.

recommended.name: Lumbar Extension-Loading Test
recommended.procedure: The examiner ensures that the lumbar region is in moderate extension (10-30 deg) while standing and patient lies supine. Check if there are changes in the symptoms that the patient feels.

recommended.procedure: Pain is reproduced on straight leg elevation for 30 seconds.

recommended.name: Lateral Lumbar Flexion (Fingertip to Floor Test)
recommended.procedure: The patient stands with heel touching wall and feet wide apart, and back against the wall. Then the examiner measures the distance from middle finger to the floor. Then patient bends to side (lateral flexion). The distance between the middle finger and the floor is measured again. This measurement is done for both sides.

recommended.name: Modified Schober's Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner marks both posterior superior iliac spine, and a horizontal line is drawn between both marks. A second line is marked 5cm below the first line, and a third line is marked 10cm above the first line. Patient is then instructed to flex forward as if attempting to touch their toes. An increase of less than 5cm shows decreased lumbar spine range of motion, and ankylosing spondylitis.

recommended.name: Spurling's Test (for Cervical Radiculitis)
recommended.procedure: While patient is seated, the examiner applies side flexion of the neck towards the affected side while applying axial compression. Sign is positive if the pain sensation felt in the shoulder-neck region is replicated.

recommended.name: Painful Arc Test
recommended.procedure: Ask patient to abduct arm across range of motion actively. Scapular rhythm is disturbed, pain is aggravated between 60-120 degrees, pain is alleviated if shoulder is laterally rotated on abduction. If positive, SIS is indicated.

recommended.name: Neer Impingement Sign
recommended.procedure: Stabilise the scapula with one hand and raise the unaffected side to full flexion with abduction and internal rotation passively. The test is positive when there is pain at the subacromial space.

recommended.name: Hawkins-Kennedy Test
recommended.procedure: Patient arm is placed in 90 deg of elevation at the scapular level and 90 deg flexion. Stabilise the upper arm with one hand and internally rotate with the other hand. The test is positive when pain is felt in the anterolateral aspect of the shoulder.

recommended.name: Jobe's Test
recommended.procedure: Elevate arm in scapular plane, extend elbow and thumb points towards floor with arm internally rotated. Patient is asked to hold the position with downward pressure from examiner. Positive sign = pain on examiner restriction indicating supraspinatus irritation.

recommended.procedure: While patient is seated, the examiner applies side flexion of the neck towards the affected side while applying axial compression. Sign is positive if the pain sensation felt in the shoulder-neck region is replicated.

recommended.name: Painful Arc Test
recommended.procedure: Ask patient to abduct arm across range of motion actively. Scapular rhythm is disturbed, pain is aggravated between 60-120 degrees, pain is alleviated if shoulder is laterally rotated on abduction. If positive, SIS is indicated.

recommended.name: Neer Impingement Sign
recommended.procedure: Stabilise the scapula with one hand and raise the unaffected side to full flexion with abduction and internal rotation passively. The test is positive when there is pain at the subacromial space.

recommended.name: Hawkins-Kennedy Test
recommended.procedure: Patient arm is placed in 90 deg of elevation at the scapular level and 90 deg flexion. Stabilise the upper arm with one hand and internally rotate with the other hand. The test is positive when pain is felt in the anterolateral aspect of the shoulder.

recommended.name: Jobe's Test
recommended.procedure: Elevate arm in scapular plane, extend elbow and thumb points towards floor with arm internally rotated. Patient is asked to hold the position with downward pressure from examiner. Positive sign = pain on examiner restriction indicating supraspinatus irritation.

recommended.name: Empty Can Test (Supraspinatus)
recommended.procedure: Patient is asked to abduct up to 90 deg, 30 deg flexion and internal rotation. Examiner stands behind patient and applies downward pressure. Positive sign: affected side is weaker than unaffected side. Positive sign suggests tear in the supraspinatus.

recommended.name: Infraspinatus Test
recommended.procedure: Patient holds arms close to body, elbow is flexed up to 90 deg of forward elevation in scapular plane. External rotation is instructed while examiner applies resistance. Lack of power on one side indicates weakness of the infraspinatus muscle.

recommended.name: Subscapularis Test (Belly Press Test)
recommended.procedure: Patient is asked to place their hand on their abdomen and move elbow forward. Patient is then asked to press hand on the abdomen. If subscapularis is torn, patient will be unable to perform movement and elbow will move backwards.

recommended.name: Lag Sign for External Rotation
recommended.procedure: Patient lifts arm slightly from body and is asked to hold in external rotation. Positive when hand recoils to neutral position and suggests tear of infraspinatus or supraspinatus.

recommended.name: Drop Sign
recommended.procedure: The examiner places the arm at 90 deg abduction, elbow at right angle and arm maximally rotated. Positive sign: arm drops from position. Suggests a tear of the infraspinatus or the posterior part of the rotator cuff.

recommended.name: Lift-Off Test (Subscapularis)
recommended.procedure: Patient is asked to place hand on the back at the mid-lumbar spine. The clinician then lifts hand from the back and patient is asked to hold it there. Positive sign: inability to maintain hand while removed suggests subscapularis weakness.

questionResponseTests.question: Have you had a previous history of a shoulder dislocation?

recommended.name: Apprehension Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is in sitting or lying position, the examiner lifts the arm gently into abduction, external rotation and then extension. Test is positive if patient senses that humeral head is about to slip out anteriorly and body stiffens in apprehension. The test is repeated with the anterior part of shoulder protected.

recommended.name: Fulcrum's Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine, arm abducted up to 90 deg. The examiner places their hands over the shoulder to set the fulcrum base. The humeral head is levered forward by extending and externally rotating arm. The patient immediately becomes apprehensive.

recommended.name: Drawer's Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine, scapula is stabilised with one hand while the upper arm is grasped firmly with the other, and manoeuvring is done forward and backward (like a drawer). The drawer's test is positive if instability is marked.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Do you feel the pain about 4 cm above your heel?

recommended.name: Ultrasound
recommended.procedure: Use ultrasound to investigate tears

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: Imaging to confirm diagnosis

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Do you feel the pain about 5cm from your heel?

recommended.name: Thompson's Test (Simmond's Test)
recommended.procedure: Patient lies prone and the calf is squeezed. If tendon is ruptured, the foot will remain still when it ought to contract involuntarily.

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Plantarflexion Weakness
recommended.procedure: Check if plantarflexion of the ankle is weak

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Palpable Gap
recommended.procedure: Check for palpable gap at the site of the rupture

recommended.name: Ultrasound
recommended.procedure: Use ultrasound to confirm the diagnosis

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Is pain and tenderness localised to the insertion of the Tendon Achilles?

recommended.name: Clinical Assessment
recommended.procedure: Physical examination and clinical assessment based on presenting symptoms

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Where do you feel the pain?

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Posterior Calcaneum
recommended.procedure: Check if the posterior portion of the calcaneum looks more prominent

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Do you experience pain on heel or sole with standing and/or walking?

recommended.name: Ultrasound
recommended.procedure: Confirmation using ultrasound to check for thickening around the heel

recommended.name: Doppler Test
recommended.procedure: Doppler test to show increased local blood flow and neovascularisation

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Did you stumble on a stairway, potholes or pavement before the onset of pain?

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Palpation
recommended.procedure: Palpate the ankle distally and anteriorly to the lateral malleolus and ask if patient feels more pain. Usually, patient feels more pain on palpation.

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: Rule out undisplaced fracture of fibula, tarsal bone, 5th metatarsal bone

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Is severe pain felt on slight attempt to invert (turn inward) foot?

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Palpation
recommended.procedure: Palpate the ankle distally and anteriorly to the lateral malleolus and ask if patient feels more pain. Usually, patient feels more pain on palpation.

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: Rule out undisplaced fracture of fibula, tarsal bone, 5th metatarsal bone

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Have you had a past episode of an ankle sprain?

recommended.name: Talar Tilt Test
recommended.procedure: The ankle is held in the neutral position, examiner stabilises the tibia just above the ankle and then tries to force the ankle into maximum inversion. The ROM can be measured or compared with the contralateral side. Inversion laxity suggests injury to calcaneofibular and anterior talofibular ligaments (ATFL).

recommended.name: Anterior Drawer Test
recommended.procedure: Patient sits with knee flexed at 90 deg and ankle in plantarflexion of about 10 deg. The lower leg is stabilised by the examiner and forces patient's heel forward over the tibia. If positive, the talus can be felt sliding forwards and backwards. Laxity indicates tear of the ATFL.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Do you have a previous history of fibular fracture?

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Foot Position
recommended.procedure: Check if foot is everted and externally rotated

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: Check for widening of the medial joint space in the mortise view, check if talus is tilted, check for fracture or dislocation of the proximal fibula

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Did you have an injury that twisted your ankle?

recommended.name: Squeeze Test
recommended.procedure: Compress the leg firmly above the ankle. Test is positive if pain is felt over the syndesmosis.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Do you play sports?

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: Confirm fracture using radiographic imaging

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Are you osteoporotic?

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: X-ray imaging to confirm fracture

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Do you feel intense pain in the foot?

recommended.name: Clinical Assessment - Foot Compartment Syndrome
recommended.procedure: Refer for laboratory confirmation

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Do you feel uncomfortable when you wear your shoes?

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Deformities
recommended.procedure: Check for the following deformities: flattened anterior arch, hallux valgus, claw toes, prominence of the metatarsal head in the soles (feels like walking on stones), presence of subcutaneous nodules

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: Check for osteoporosis and periarticular erosion at the metatarsophalangeal joint

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Do you find it increasingly difficult to walk?

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: Check for osteoporosis, erosion of the tarsal and ankle joints and the swelling of soft-tissues

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Have you had a previous diagnosis of osteoarthritis of other joints?

recommended.name: Clinical Assessment
recommended.procedure: Physical examination and clinical assessment based on presenting symptoms

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Do you feel numbness, burning and tingling sensation in your foot and/or medial portion of your ankle?

recommended.name: Tinel's Sign
recommended.procedure: Percussion of the tarsal tunnel. Positive if this results in a distal radiation of paraesthesia.

recommended.name: Dorsiflexion-Eversion Test
recommended.procedure: Place the patient's foot into dorsiflexion and eversion and hold for 5-10 seconds. Positive if patient's symptom is elicited.

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Abductor Hallucis
recommended.procedure: Check for atrophy of the abductor hallucis

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Arch Stability
recommended.procedure: Check for arch stability

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Talus and Calcaneus Position
recommended.procedure: Check for the position of the talus and calcaneus

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Where is your pain worse?

recommended.name: Spurling's Test (Maximal Cervical Compression and Foraminal Compression Test)
recommended.procedure: The neck is placed in extension, lateral flexion, and axial compression. The test is positive if pain is present and radiates to the arm.

recommended.name: Cervical Distraction Test
recommended.procedure: The patient lies supine and the neck is positioned comfortably. The examiner places hand around the patient's mastoid process. The examiner then slightly flexes the patient's neck and pulls the head towards your torso. Test is positive if the symptoms reduce or are eliminated with traction.

recommended.name: MRI
recommended.procedure: Radiographic confirmation of disc herniation

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Cervical Rotation
recommended.procedure: Check if cervical rotation on the affected side is less than 60 degrees

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Where is your pain worse?

recommended.name: Spurling's Test (Maximal Cervical Compression and Foraminal Compression Test)
recommended.procedure: The neck is placed in extension, lateral flexion, and axial compression. The test is positive if pain is present and radiates to the arm.

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: Check for loss of normal cervical lordosis, and degeneration

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: What region is pain present in?

recommended.name: Cozen’s Test
recommended.procedure: Patient makes a fist, pronates forearm, and extends wrist against examiner resistance with elbow in 90° flexion.

recommended.name: Mill’s Sign
recommended.procedure: Patient closes hand, examiner fully extends elbow, pronates forearm, and flexes wrist.

recommended.name: Maudsley’s Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner resists extension of middle finger (third digit) distal to PIP joint.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Do you experience pain, numbness or abnormal sensation in the forearm, fourth and ring finger?

recommended.name: Tinel’s Sign at Cubital Tunnel
recommended.procedure: Examiner lightly taps ulnar nerve in groove between medial epicondyle and olecranon.

recommended.name: Elbow Flexion Test
recommended.procedure: Patient holds elbow in maximal flexion with wrist in neutral for up to 3 minutes.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Do you exercise often by lifting weights?

recommended.name: Valgus Stress Test
recommended.procedure: Forearm supinated, elbow flexed to 25°–30°. Examiner stabilizes arm and applies valgus stress to forearm.

recommended.name: Moving Valgus Stress Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner applies constant valgus torque while flexing and extending elbow between 30° and 120°.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Is a nodule present at the back of the elbow?

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: Check for osteopenia, bone erosions, destruction of the radial head and widening of the sigmoid notch

recommended.name: Laboratory Tests
recommended.procedure: Other laboratory tests as may be necessary (RF, anti-CCP, ESR, CRP)

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Do you work a manual job?

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: Check for joint space narrowing, osteophyte formation, and subchondral sclerosis

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Where is the pain located?

recommended.name: FABER Test (Patrick’s Test)
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Affected leg is placed in flexion, abduction, and external rotation (figure-4). Examiner applies gentle downward pressure on knee while stabilizing opposite ASIS.

recommended.name: FADIR Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes hip to 90°, then adducts and internally rotates hip.

recommended.name: Scour Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes and adducts hip, applies axial compression along femur while sweeping hip in an arc between adduction/internal rotation and abduction/external rotation.

recommended.name: Log Roll Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with legs extended. Examiner gently rolls the entire leg into internal and external rotation.

recommended.name: Trendelenburg Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands unsupported on affected leg for 30 seconds. Examiner observes pelvic tilt.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Where is the pain located?

recommended.name: Single-Leg Stance Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands on affected leg unsupported for up to 30 seconds.

recommended.name: Resisted External Derotation Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine with hip and knee flexed to 90°. Examiner passively externally rotates hip, then asks patient to return to neutral against resistance.

recommended.name: Ober’s Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies on unaffected side. Examiner extends and abducts affected hip, then allows leg to drop into adduction.

recommended.name: Trendelenburg Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands on affected leg while examiner observes contralateral pelvic level.

recommended.name: Greater Trochanter Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner applies firm direct palpation over lateral greater trochanter and gluteal tendon insertions.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Where is the pain located?

recommended.name: FADIR Test (Flexion, Adduction, Internal Rotation)
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes hip to 90°, then adducts and internally rotates the hip.

recommended.name: FABER Test (Patrick’s Test)
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with foot on opposite knee (figure-4). Examiner applies downward pressure on ipsilateral knee.

recommended.name: Scour Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes and adducts hip, then applies axial compression while sweeping in an arc.

recommended.name: Internal Rotation Overpressure Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with hip flexed to 90°. Examiner applies internal rotation with terminal overpressure.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Where is the pain located?

recommended.name: FADIR Test (Labral Impingement)
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner passively flexes, adducts, and internally rotates hip.

recommended.name: Scour Test (Axial Load)
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner applies axial load through femur while moving hip in circular compression arcs.

recommended.name: Log Roll Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with legs extended. Examiner gently rolls leg into full internal and external rotation.

recommended.name: Modified Thomas Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine at edge of table, pulling one knee to chest while affected leg hangs extended.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Where is the pain located?

recommended.name: Log Roll Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with legs extended. Examiner gently rolls the leg internally and externally.

recommended.name: FADIR Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes, adducts, and internally rotates hip.

recommended.name: FABER Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine in figure-4 position. Examiner applies downward pressure on knee.

recommended.name: MRI of Bilateral Hips (Gold Standard)
recommended.procedure: T1/T2-weighted MRI of pelvis and both femoral heads.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Where is the snapping located?

recommended.name: Dynamic Hip Movement Test
recommended.procedure: Patient actively flexes, abducts, and externally rotates hip, then returns to extension and adduction while examiner palpates.

recommended.name: Ober’s Test (External Snapping)
recommended.procedure: Patient lies on side. Examiner extends and abducts affected hip, then allows leg to drop toward table.

recommended.name: Thomas Test (Internal Snapping)
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine holding opposite knee to chest while affected hip is extended from flexion.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: What region is pain present in?

recommended.name: Resisted Quadriceps Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is seated with knee slightly flexed. Examiner applies resistance as the patient extends the knee.

recommended.name: Step-Down Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands on a 20 cm step and slowly lowers contralateral heel to the ground while examiner observes alignment.

recommended.name: Clarke’s Test (Patellar Grind Test)
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with knee extended. Examiner applies gentle downward pressure on superior pole of patella while patient contracts quadriceps.

recommended.name: Patellar Apprehension Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine and relaxed. Examiner pushes the patella laterally.

recommended.name: Patellar Tilt Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with knee extended. Examiner lifts the lateral edge of the patella.

recommended.name: Waldron Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is seated and actively flexes and extends knee while examiner palpates patellofemoral joint.

recommended.name: Patellar Glide Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with knee extended. Examiner glides patella medially and laterally.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Do you have recent twisting injury?

recommended.name: McMurray Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes the hip and knee fully, then rotates the tibia internally and externally while extending the knee.

recommended.name: Apley’s Compression Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies prone with knee flexed to 90°. Examiner applies downward axial pressure along tibia while rotating it internally and externally.

recommended.name: Thessaly Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands on one leg with knee flexed to 20°. Patient rotates body and knee internally and externally three times.

recommended.name: Joint Line Tenderness Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates along medial and lateral tibiofemoral joint lines with knee flexed to 90°.

recommended.name: Bounce Home Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner fully flexes the knee and then allows it to passively extend.

recommended.name: Ege’s Test
recommended.procedure: Patient squats with knees flexed and externally rotates feet (medial meniscus) or internally rotates feet (lateral meniscus).

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: How did the pain begin?

recommended.name: Resisted Contraction Test
recommended.procedure: Patient contracts the affected muscle against examiner resistance at mid-range.

recommended.name: Crepitus Assessment (Full ROM)
recommended.procedure: Examiner moves knee through full active and passive flexion and extension while palpating joint.

recommended.name: Joint Line Tenderness
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates medial and lateral tibiofemoral joint lines.

recommended.name: Functional Pain Assessment

recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine with knee extended. Examiner gently pushes patella laterally.

recommended.procedure: Observe patella motion during active knee flexion and extension.

recommended.name: Patellar Hypermobility Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine, knee extended. Examiner gently displaces patella medially and laterally.

recommended.name: Q-Angle Measurement
recommended.procedure: Measure angle between ASIS-to-patella center line and patella-to-tibial-tuberosity line with knee extended.

recommended.name: Observation for Patella Alta / Genu Recurvatum
recommended.procedure: Inspect patellar height in full extension (Insall-Salvati ratio) and assess knee hyperextension.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Do you have recent fall, RTA, or high-impact trauma?

recommended.name: Active Straight Leg Raise Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine with legs extended. Examiner asks patient to lift affected leg straight up without bending knee.

recommended.name: Patellar Tap / Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine with knee relaxed. Examiner palpates patella gently feeling for gap, step-off, or bone fragment displacement.

recommended.name: Ottawa Knee Rules Assessment
recommended.procedure: Assess age (≥55), isolated patellar tenderness, fibular head tenderness, flexion <90°, or inability to bear weight 4 steps.

recommended.name: Tibial Plateau Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Palpate medial and lateral tibial condyles and tibial plateau margins.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Does your activity involve repetitive knee bending (running, cycling)?

recommended.name: Noble’s Compression Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine. Examiner flexes knee to 90° and applies pressure over lateral femoral epicondyle while slowly extending knee.

recommended.name: Ober’s Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies on unaffected side. Examiner extends and abducts hip, then slowly lowers the leg into adduction.

recommended.name: Renne’s Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands on affected leg and performs single-leg squat while examiner applies pressure over lateral femoral epicondyle.

recommended.name: Modified Thomas Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine at edge of table, hugging contralateral knee to chest. Examiner assesses affected thigh position.

recommended.name: Lateral Epicondyle Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates lateral femoral epicondyle with knee moved between 0° and 90° flexion.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Does your activity involves jumping, sprinting, or frequent knee loading?

recommended.name: Decline Squat Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands on a 25° decline board and performs double- or single-leg squat.

recommended.name: Resisted Knee Extension Test
recommended.procedure: Patient sits with knee flexed. Examiner applies isometric resistance to knee extension.

recommended.name: Single-Leg Decline Squat Test
recommended.procedure: Patient performs single-leg squat on a 25° decline board, loading the extensor mechanism.

recommended.name: Patellar Tendon Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates inferior pole of patella and body of patellar tendon with knee extended and flexed.

recommended.name: Single-Leg Hop Test
recommended.procedure: Patient performs repeated hops on the affected leg.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Where is the pain located ?

recommended.name: Pes Anserinus Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine with knee extended. Examiner palpates anteromedial proximal tibia, 5–7 cm below medial joint line.

recommended.name: Resisted Knee Flexion Test
recommended.procedure: Patient flexes knee from 90° while examiner applies manual resistance.

recommended.name: Resisted Hip Adduction Test
recommended.procedure: Patient performs hip adduction against examiner resistance.

recommended.name: Hamstring Stretch Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner passively extends knee with hip flexed, stretching hamstring tendons.

recommended.name: Joint Line Differentiation Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates medial joint line and pes anserine region sequentially.

conditionSummary.firstQuestion: Where is the pain located?

recommended.name: Wilson’s Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine. Examiner flexes knee to 90°. Patient actively extends knee while examiner internally rotates tibia.

recommended.name: Passive Condylar Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Patient knee flexed to 90°. Examiner palpates femoral condyles directly through flexed joint.

recommended.name: Joint Effusion Test (Stroke Test)
recommended.procedure: Examiner strokes medial knee upward and lateral knee downward to evaluate fluid bulge.

recommended.name: Single-Leg Squat Loading Test
recommended.procedure: Patient performs single-leg squat on affected leg.

recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates medial aspect of popliteal fossa between semimembranosus and medial gastrocnemius head.

recommended.name: Transillumination Test
recommended.procedure: Light source placed against posterior knee swelling in a dimmed examination room.

recommended.name: Knee Effusion Stroke Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner performs sweep/stroke test across medial and lateral parapatellar gutters.

recommended.name: Joint Effusion Test (Bulge / Ballottement Test)
recommended.procedure: Examiner applies downward pressure on suprapatellar pouch and ballottes patella against femur.

recommended.name: Diagnostic Arthrocentesis (Gold Standard)

recommended.procedure: Examiner raises legs of patient up so that hip flexion is achieved while knee is extended. Test is positive if patient feels pain along the course of the sciatic nerve and below the knee when hip is between 30-70 degrees of flexion.

recommended.name: Two-stage Treadmill Test
recommended.procedure: The patient walks on a flat treadmill and the amount of time spent is recorded and compared with the amount of time while the treadmill is inclined such that patient walks in flexion.

recommended.name: Lumbar Extension-Loading Test
recommended.procedure: The examiner ensures that the lumbar region is in moderate extension (10-30 deg) while standing and patient lies supine. Check if there are changes in the symptoms that the patient feels.

recommended.name: Lateral Lumbar Flexion (Fingertip to Floor Test)
recommended.procedure: The patient stands with heel touching wall and feet wide apart, and back against the wall. Then the examiner measures the distance from middle finger to the floor. Then patient bends to side (lateral flexion). The distance between the middle finger and the floor is measured again. This measurement is done for both sides.

recommended.name: Modified Schober's Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner marks both posterior superior iliac spine, and a horizontal line is drawn between both marks. A second line is marked 5cm below the first line, and a third line is marked 10cm above the first line. Patient is then instructed to flex forward as if attempting to touch their toes. An increase of less than 5cm shows decreased lumbar spine range of motion, and ankylosing spondylitis.

recommended.name: Chest Expansion Test
recommended.procedure: Normal chest expansion is ≥ 5 cm

recommended.name: Occiput to Wall Distance
recommended.procedure: Normal distance is 0

recommended.name: Tragus to Wall Distance
recommended.procedure: Normal distance is < 15cm

recommended.name: Intermalleolar Distance

recommended.name: Spurling's Test (for Cervical Radiculitis)
recommended.procedure: While patient is seated, the examiner applies side flexion of the neck towards the affected side while applying axial compression. Sign is positive if the pain sensation felt in the shoulder-neck region is replicated.

recommended.name: Painful Arc Test
recommended.procedure: Ask patient to abduct arm across range of motion actively. Scapular rhythm is disturbed, pain is aggravated between 60-120 degrees, pain is alleviated if shoulder is laterally rotated on abduction. If positive, SIS is indicated.

recommended.name: Neer Impingement Sign
recommended.procedure: Stabilise the scapula with one hand and raise the unaffected side to full flexion with abduction and internal rotation passively. The test is positive when there is pain at the subacromial space.

recommended.name: Hawkins-Kennedy Test
recommended.procedure: Patient arm is placed in 90 deg of elevation at the scapular level and 90 deg flexion. Stabilise the upper arm with one hand and internally rotate with the other hand. The test is positive when pain is felt in the anterolateral aspect of the shoulder.

recommended.name: Jobe's Test
recommended.procedure: Elevate arm in scapular plane, extend elbow and thumb points towards floor with arm internally rotated. Patient is asked to hold the position with downward pressure from examiner. Positive sign = pain on examiner restriction indicating supraspinatus irritation.

recommended.name: Empty Can Test (Supraspinatus)
recommended.procedure: Patient is asked to abduct up to 90 deg, 30 deg flexion and internal rotation. Examiner stands behind patient and applies downward pressure. Positive sign: affected side is weaker than unaffected side. Positive sign suggests tear in the supraspinatus.

recommended.name: Infraspinatus Test
recommended.procedure: Patient holds arms close to body, elbow is flexed up to 90 deg of forward elevation in scapular plane. External rotation is instructed while examiner applies resistance. Lack of power on one side indicates weakness of the infraspinatus muscle.

recommended.name: Subscapularis Test (Belly Press Test)
recommended.procedure: Patient is asked to place their hand on their abdomen and move elbow forward. Patient is then asked to press hand on the abdomen. If subscapularis is torn, patient will be unable to perform movement and elbow will move backwards.

recommended.name: Lag Sign for External Rotation
recommended.procedure: Patient lifts arm slightly from body and is asked to hold in external rotation. Positive when hand recoils to neutral position and suggests tear of infraspinatus or supraspinatus.

recommended.name: Drop Sign
recommended.procedure: The examiner places the arm at 90 deg abduction, elbow at right angle and arm maximally rotated. Positive sign: arm drops from position. Suggests a tear of the infraspinatus or the posterior part of the rotator cuff.

recommended.name: Lift-Off Test (Subscapularis)
recommended.procedure: Patient is asked to place hand on the back at the mid-lumbar spine. The clinician then lifts hand from the back and patient is asked to hold it there. Positive sign: inability to maintain hand while removed suggests subscapularis weakness.

recommended.name: Apprehension Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is in sitting or lying position, the examiner lifts the arm gently into abduction, external rotation and then extension. Test is positive if patient senses that humeral head is about to slip out anteriorly and body stiffens in apprehension. The test is repeated with the anterior part of shoulder protected.

recommended.name: Fulcrum's Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine, arm abducted up to 90 deg. The examiner places their hands over the shoulder to set the fulcrum base. The humeral head is levered forward by extending and externally rotating arm. The patient immediately becomes apprehensive.

recommended.name: Drawer's Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine, scapula is stabilised with one hand while the upper arm is grasped firmly with the other, and manoeuvring is done forward and backward (like a drawer). The drawer's test is positive if instability is marked.

The lower leg is stabilised by the examiner and forces patient's heel forward over the tibia. If positive, the talus can be felt sliding forwards and backwards. Laxity indicates tear of the ATFL.

recommended.procedure: Check if cervical rotation on the affected side is less than 60 degrees

recommended.name: Spurling's Test (Maximal Cervical Compression and Foraminal Compression Test)
recommended.procedure: The neck is placed in extension, lateral flexion, and axial compression. The test is positive if pain is present and radiates to the arm.

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: Check for loss of normal cervical lordosis, and degeneration

recommended.name: Cozen’s Test
recommended.procedure: Patient makes a fist, pronates forearm, and extends wrist against examiner resistance with elbow in 90° flexion.

recommended.name: Mill’s Sign
recommended.procedure: Patient closes hand, examiner fully extends elbow, pronates forearm, and flexes wrist.

recommended.name: Maudsley’s Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner resists extension of middle finger (third digit) distal to PIP joint.

recommended.name: Tinel’s Sign at Cubital Tunnel
recommended.procedure: Examiner lightly taps ulnar nerve in groove between medial epicondyle and olecranon.

recommended.name: Elbow Flexion Test
recommended.procedure: Patient holds elbow in maximal flexion with wrist in neutral for up to 3 minutes.

recommended.name: Valgus Stress Test
recommended.procedure: Forearm supinated, elbow flexed to 25°–30°. Examiner stabilizes arm and applies valgus stress to forearm.

recommended.name: Moving Valgus Stress Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner applies constant valgus torque while flexing and extending elbow between 30° and 120°.

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: Check for osteopenia, bone erosions, destruction of the radial head and widening of the sigmoid notch

recommended.name: Laboratory Tests
recommended.procedure: Other laboratory tests as may be necessary (RF, anti-CCP, ESR, CRP)

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: Check for joint space narrowing, osteophyte formation, and subchondral sclerosis

recommended.name: FABER Test (Patrick’s Test)
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Affected leg is placed in flexion, abduction, and external rotation (figure-4). Examiner applies gentle downward pressure on knee while stabilizing opposite ASIS.

recommended.name: FADIR Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes hip to 90°, then adducts and internally rotates hip.

recommended.name: Scour Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes and adducts hip, applies axial compression along femur while sweeping hip in an arc between adduction/internal rotation and abduction/external rotation.

recommended.name: Log Roll Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with legs extended. Examiner gently rolls the entire leg into internal and external rotation.

recommended.name: Trendelenburg Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands unsupported on affected leg for 30 seconds. Examiner observes pelvic tilt.

recommended.name: Single-Leg Stance Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands on affected leg unsupported for up to 30 seconds.

recommended.name: Resisted External Derotation Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine with hip and knee flexed to 90°. Examiner passively externally rotates hip, then asks patient to return to neutral against resistance.

recommended.name: Ober’s Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies on unaffected side. Examiner extends and abducts affected hip, then allows leg to drop into adduction.

recommended.name: Trendelenburg Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands on affected leg while examiner observes contralateral pelvic level.

recommended.name: Greater Trochanter Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner applies firm direct palpation over lateral greater trochanter and gluteal tendon insertions.

recommended.name: FADIR Test (Flexion, Adduction, Internal Rotation)
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes hip to 90°, then adducts and internally rotates the hip.

recommended.name: FABER Test (Patrick’s Test)
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with foot on opposite knee (figure-4). Examiner applies downward pressure on ipsilateral knee.

recommended.name: Scour Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes and adducts hip, then applies axial compression while sweeping in an arc.

recommended.name: Internal Rotation Overpressure Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with hip flexed to 90°. Examiner applies internal rotation with terminal overpressure.

recommended.name: FADIR Test (Labral Impingement)
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner passively flexes, adducts, and internally rotates hip.

recommended.name: Scour Test (Axial Load)
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner applies axial load through femur while moving hip in circular compression arcs.

recommended.name: Log Roll Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with legs extended. Examiner gently rolls leg into full internal and external rotation.

recommended.name: Modified Thomas Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine at edge of table, pulling one knee to chest while affected leg hangs extended.

recommended.name: Log Roll Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with legs extended. Examiner gently rolls the leg internally and externally.

recommended.name: FADIR Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes, adducts, and internally rotates hip.

recommended.name: FABER Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine in figure-4 position. Examiner applies downward pressure on knee.

recommended.name: MRI of Bilateral Hips (Gold Standard)
recommended.procedure: T1/T2-weighted MRI of pelvis and both femoral heads.

recommended.name: Dynamic Hip Movement Test
recommended.procedure: Patient actively flexes, abducts, and externally rotates hip, then returns to extension and adduction while examiner palpates.

recommended.name: Ober’s Test (External Snapping)
recommended.procedure: Patient lies on side. Examiner extends and abducts affected hip, then allows leg to drop toward table.

recommended.name: Thomas Test (Internal Snapping)
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine holding opposite knee to chest while affected hip is extended from flexion.

recommended.name: Resisted Quadriceps Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is seated with knee slightly flexed. Examiner applies resistance as the patient extends the knee.

recommended.name: Step-Down Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands on a 20 cm step and slowly lowers contralateral heel to the ground while examiner observes alignment.

recommended.name: Clarke’s Test (Patellar Grind Test)
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with knee extended. Examiner applies gentle downward pressure on superior pole of patella while patient contracts quadriceps.

recommended.name: Patellar Apprehension Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine and relaxed. Examiner pushes the patella laterally.

recommended.name: Patellar Tilt Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with knee extended. Examiner lifts the lateral edge of the patella.

recommended.name: Waldron Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is seated and actively flexes and extends knee while examiner palpates patellofemoral joint.

recommended.name: Patellar Glide Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine with knee extended. Examiner glides patella medially and laterally.

recommended.name: McMurray Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner flexes the hip and knee fully, then rotates the tibia internally and externally while extending the knee.

recommended.name: Apley’s Compression Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies prone with knee flexed to 90°. Examiner applies downward axial pressure along tibia while rotating it internally and externally.

recommended.name: Thessaly Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands on one leg with knee flexed to 20°. Patient rotates body and knee internally and externally three times.

recommended.name: Joint Line Tenderness Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates along medial and lateral tibiofemoral joint lines with knee flexed to 90°.

recommended.name: Bounce Home Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is supine. Examiner fully flexes the knee and then allows it to passively extend.

recommended.name: Ege’s Test
recommended.procedure: Patient squats with knees flexed and externally rotates feet (medial meniscus) or internally rotates feet (lateral meniscus).

recommended.name: Resisted Contraction Test
recommended.procedure: Patient contracts the affected muscle against examiner resistance at mid-range.

recommended.name: Passive Stretch Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner stretches the affected muscle slowly into its lengthened position.

recommended.name: Patellar Grind Test (Clarke’s Test)
recommended.procedure: Patient supine with knee extended. Examiner applies downward pressure on patella while patient contracts quadriceps.

recommended.name: Passive Patellar Tilt Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner lifts lateral edge of patella while stabilizing medial edge.

recommended.name: Crepitus Assessment (Full ROM)
recommended.procedure: Examiner moves knee through full active and passive flexion and extension while palpating joint.

recommended.name: Joint Line Tenderness
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates medial and lateral tibiofemoral joint lines.

recommended.name: Functional Pain Assessment
recommended.procedure: Ask patient to perform loaded activities such as squatting, step-ups, or sit-to-stand.

recommended.name: Patella Apprehension Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine with knee extended. Examiner gently pushes patella laterally.

recommended.name: Patella Tracking Assessment
recommended.procedure: Observe patella motion during active knee flexion and extension.

recommended.name: Patellar Hypermobility Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine, knee extended. Examiner gently displaces patella medially and laterally.

recommended.name: Q-Angle Measurement
recommended.procedure: Measure angle between ASIS-to-patella center line and patella-to-tibial-tuberosity line with knee extended.

recommended.name: Observation for Patella Alta / Genu Recurvatum
recommended.procedure: Inspect patellar height in full extension (Insall-Salvati ratio) and assess knee hyperextension.

recommended.name: Active Straight Leg Raise Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine with legs extended. Examiner asks patient to lift affected leg straight up without bending knee.

recommended.name: Patellar Tap / Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine with knee relaxed. Examiner palpates patella gently feeling for gap, step-off, or bone fragment displacement.

recommended.name: Ottawa Knee Rules Assessment
recommended.procedure: Assess age (≥55), isolated patellar tenderness, fibular head tenderness, flexion <90°, or inability to bear weight 4 steps.

recommended.name: Tibial Plateau Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Palpate medial and lateral tibial condyles and tibial plateau margins.

recommended.name: Noble’s Compression Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine. Examiner flexes knee to 90° and applies pressure over lateral femoral epicondyle while slowly extending knee.

recommended.name: Ober’s Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies on unaffected side. Examiner extends and abducts hip, then slowly lowers the leg into adduction.

recommended.name: Renne’s Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands on affected leg and performs single-leg squat while examiner applies pressure over lateral femoral epicondyle.

recommended.name: Modified Thomas Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine at edge of table, hugging contralateral knee to chest. Examiner assesses affected thigh position.

recommended.name: Lateral Epicondyle Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates lateral femoral epicondyle with knee moved between 0° and 90° flexion.

recommended.name: Decline Squat Test
recommended.procedure: Patient stands on a 25° decline board and performs double- or single-leg squat.

recommended.name: Resisted Knee Extension Test
recommended.procedure: Patient sits with knee flexed. Examiner applies isometric resistance to knee extension.

recommended.name: Single-Leg Decline Squat Test
recommended.procedure: Patient performs single-leg squat on a 25° decline board, loading the extensor mechanism.

recommended.name: Patellar Tendon Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates inferior pole of patella and body of patellar tendon with knee extended and flexed.

recommended.name: Single-Leg Hop Test
recommended.procedure: Patient performs repeated hops on the affected leg.

recommended.name: Pes Anserinus Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine with knee extended. Examiner palpates anteromedial proximal tibia, 5–7 cm below medial joint line.

recommended.name: Resisted Knee Flexion Test
recommended.procedure: Patient flexes knee from 90° while examiner applies manual resistance.

recommended.name: Resisted Hip Adduction Test
recommended.procedure: Patient performs hip adduction against examiner resistance.

recommended.name: Hamstring Stretch Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner passively extends knee with hip flexed, stretching hamstring tendons.

recommended.name: Joint Line Differentiation Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates medial joint line and pes anserine region sequentially.

recommended.name: Wilson’s Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine. Examiner flexes knee to 90°. Patient actively extends knee while examiner internally rotates tibia.

recommended.name: Passive Condylar Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Patient knee flexed to 90°. Examiner palpates femoral condyles directly through flexed joint.

recommended.name: Joint Effusion Test (Stroke Test)
recommended.procedure: Examiner strokes medial knee upward and lateral knee downward to evaluate fluid bulge.

recommended.name: Single-Leg Squat Loading Test
recommended.procedure: Patient performs single-leg squat on affected leg.

recommended.name: Foucher’s Sign
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine. Examiner palpates popliteal mass with knee fully extended, then with knee flexed to 45°.

recommended.name: Popliteal Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates medial aspect of popliteal fossa between semimembranosus and medial gastrocnemius head.

recommended.name: Transillumination Test
recommended.procedure: Light source placed against posterior knee swelling in a dimmed examination room.

recommended.name: Knee Effusion Stroke Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner performs sweep/stroke test across medial and lateral parapatellar gutters.

recommended.name: Passive Joint Motion Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner gently moves patient’s knee through minimal passive flexion and extension.

recommended.name: Local Temperature Assessment
recommended.procedure: Examiner uses dorsum of hand to compare skin temperature of affected knee to contralateral knee.

recommended.name: Joint Effusion Test (Bulge / Ballottement Test)
recommended.procedure: Examiner applies downward pressure on suprapatellar pouch and ballottes patella against femur.

recommended.name: Diagnostic Arthrocentesis (Gold Standard)
recommended.procedure: Sterile needle joint aspiration for synovial fluid WBC count, Gram stain, crystals, and culture.

recommended.name: Lasègue's Test (Straight-Leg Raise)
recommended.procedure: Examiner raises legs of patient up so that hip flexion is achieved while knee is extended. Test is positive if patient feels pain along the course of the sciatic nerve and below the knee when hip is between 30-70 degrees of flexion.

recommended.name: Bragard Test
recommended.procedure: This is a modification of the SLR and dorsiflexion is applied at the end of the SLR. This reduces the angle where the test is positive.

recommended.name: Lasègue's Test (Straight-Leg Raise)
recommended.procedure: Examiner raises legs of patient up so that hip flexion is achieved while knee is extended. Test is positive if patient feels pain along the course of the sciatic nerve and below the knee when hip is between 30-70 degrees of flexion.

recommended.name: Bragard Test
recommended.procedure: This is a modification of the SLR and dorsiflexion is applied at the end of the SLR. This reduces the angle where the test is positive.

recommended.name: Bowstring Test (Popliteal Compression Test / Tibial Nerve Stretch Sign)
recommended.procedure: This can be done while patient is lying in supine or sitting position. The examiner flexes the knee and applies pressure on the popliteal fossa evoking sciatica.

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Knee Jerk Reflex
recommended.procedure: Check if knee jerk reflex is present

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Ankle Jerk Reflex
recommended.procedure: Check if ankle jerk reflex is present

recommended.name: Bicycle Stress Test
recommended.procedure: Record the amount of time the patient spends on a cycle ergometer while in a neutral lumbar position and slumped position. If patient spends more time in the slumped position, a lumbar spinal stenosis is indicated.

recommended.name: Two-stage Treadmill Test
recommended.procedure: The patient walks on a flat treadmill and the amount of time spent is recorded and compared with the amount of time while the treadmill is inclined such that patient walks in flexion.

recommended.name: Lumbar Extension-Loading Test
recommended.procedure: The examiner ensures that the lumbar region is in moderate extension (10-30 deg) while standing and patient lies supine. Check if there are changes in the symptoms that the patient feels.

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Wide-based Gait
recommended.procedure: Check if a wide-based gait is present

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Trendelenburg's Sign
recommended.procedure: Check if Trendelenburg's sign is present

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Romberg Test
recommended.procedure: Check for negative Romberg test

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Achilles Reflex
recommended.procedure: Check if Achilles tendon reflex is diminished

recommended.name: Lasègue's Test (Straight-Leg Raise)
recommended.procedure: Examiner raises legs of patient up so that hip flexion is achieved while knee is extended. Test is positive if patient feels pain along the course of the sciatic nerve and below the knee when hip is between 30-70 degrees of flexion.

recommended.name: Bragard Test
recommended.procedure: This is a modification of the SLR and dorsiflexion is applied at the end of the SLR. This reduces the angle where the test is positive.

recommended.name: Bowstring Test (Popliteal Compression Test / Tibial Nerve Stretch Sign)
recommended.procedure: This can be done while patient is lying in supine or sitting position. The examiner flexes the knee and applies pressure on the popliteal fossa evoking sciatica.

recommended.name: Femoral Nerve Stretch Test (Wasserman Sign)
recommended.procedure: Patient is in prone position, knee is flexed and hip is extended. Reproduction of pain in anterior thigh is positive.

recommended.name: Kernig Test
recommended.procedure: Patient's neck is flexed, hip flexed and the leg is extended. Pain is reproduced in this position.

recommended.name: Milgram Test
recommended.procedure: Pain is reproduced on straight leg elevation for 30 seconds.

recommended.name: MRI
recommended.procedure: Radiographic confirmation of disc herniation

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Paraspinal Tenderness
recommended.procedure: Check for tenderness in the paraspinal musculature

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Paraspinal Spasms
recommended.procedure: Check for spasms in the paraspinal musculature

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Decreased Reflexes
recommended.procedure: Check for decreased reflexes: patellar and ankle jerk

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Trendelenburg's Sign
recommended.procedure: Check for Trendelenburg's sign

recommended.name: MRI
recommended.procedure: Radiographic confirmation - urgent imaging required

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Upper Motor Neuron Signs
recommended.procedure: Check for Babinski sign and clonus to rule out upper motor neuron involvement

recommended.name: Lateral Lumbar Flexion (Fingertip to Floor Test)
recommended.procedure: The patient stands with heel touching wall and feet wide apart, and back against the wall. Then the examiner measures the distance from middle finger to the floor. Then patient bends to side (lateral flexion). The distance between the middle finger and the floor is measured again. This measurement is done for both sides.

recommended.name: Modified Schober's Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner marks both posterior superior iliac spine, and a horizontal line is drawn between both marks. A second line is marked 5cm below the first line, and a third line is marked 10cm above the first line. Patient is then instructed to flex forward as if attempting to touch their toes. An increase of less than 5cm shows decreased lumbar spine range of motion, and ankylosing spondylitis.

recommended.name: Chest Expansion Test
recommended.procedure: Normal chest expansion is ≥ 5 cm

recommended.name: Occiput to Wall Distance
recommended.procedure: Normal distance is 0

recommended.name: Tragus to Wall Distance
recommended.procedure: Normal distance is < 15cm

recommended.name: Intermalleolar Distance
recommended.procedure: Normal distance is > 100cm

recommended.name: Laboratory Investigations
recommended.procedure: Confirmatory test through laboratory investigations (HLA-B27, ESR, CRP)

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: X-ray to check for fracture location and displacement

recommended.name: Spurling's Test (for Cervical Radiculitis)
recommended.procedure: While patient is seated, the examiner applies side flexion of the neck towards the affected side while applying axial compression. Sign is positive if the pain sensation felt in the shoulder-neck region is replicated.

recommended.name: Painful Arc Test
recommended.procedure: Ask patient to abduct arm across range of motion actively. Scapular rhythm is disturbed, pain is aggravated between 60-120 degrees, pain is alleviated if shoulder is laterally rotated on abduction. If positive, SIS is indicated.

recommended.name: Neer Impingement Sign
recommended.procedure: Stabilise the scapula with one hand and raise the unaffected side to full flexion with abduction and internal rotation passively. The test is positive when there is pain at the subacromial space.

recommended.name: Hawkins-Kennedy Test
recommended.procedure: Patient arm is placed in 90 deg of elevation at the scapular level and 90 deg flexion. Stabilise the upper arm with one hand and internally rotate with the other hand. The test is positive when pain is felt in the anterolateral aspect of the shoulder.

recommended.name: Jobe's Test
recommended.procedure: Elevate arm in scapular plane, extend elbow and thumb points towards floor with arm internally rotated. Patient is asked to hold the position with downward pressure from examiner. Positive sign = pain on examiner restriction indicating supraspinatus irritation.

recommended.name: Clinical Assessment
recommended.procedure: Physical examination and clinical assessment based on presenting symptoms

recommended.name: Clinical Observation - Bicipital Groove
recommended.procedure: Check for tenderness along the bicipital groove or on moving the biceps tendon (bicipital tendinitis can co-exist with other rotator cuff pathologies)

recommended.name: Empty Can Test (Supraspinatus)
recommended.procedure: Patient is asked to abduct up to 90 deg, 30 deg flexion and internal rotation. Examiner stands behind patient and applies downward pressure. Positive sign: affected side is weaker than unaffected side. Positive sign suggests tear in the supraspinatus.

recommended.name: Infraspinatus Test
recommended.procedure: Patient holds arms close to body, elbow is flexed up to 90 deg of forward elevation in scapular plane. External rotation is instructed while examiner applies resistance. Lack of power on one side indicates weakness of the infraspinatus muscle.

recommended.name: Subscapularis Test (Belly Press Test)
recommended.procedure: Patient is asked to place their hand on their abdomen and move elbow forward. Patient is then asked to press hand on the abdomen. If subscapularis is torn, patient will be unable to perform movement and elbow will move backwards.

recommended.name: Lag Sign for External Rotation
recommended.procedure: Patient lifts arm slightly from body and is asked to hold in external rotation. Positive when hand recoils to neutral position and suggests tear of infraspinatus or supraspinatus.

recommended.name: Drop Sign
recommended.procedure: The examiner places the arm at 90 deg abduction, elbow at right angle and arm maximally rotated. Positive sign: arm drops from position. Suggests a tear of the infraspinatus or the posterior part of the rotator cuff.

recommended.name: Lift-Off Test (Subscapularis)
recommended.procedure: Patient is asked to place hand on the back at the mid-lumbar spine. The clinician then lifts hand from the back and patient is asked to hold it there. Positive sign: inability to maintain hand while removed suggests subscapularis weakness.

recommended.name: X-ray
recommended.procedure: Check X-ray to rule out asymptomatic calcification

recommended.name: Apprehension Test
recommended.procedure: Patient is in sitting or lying position, the examiner lifts the arm gently into abduction, external rotation and then extension. Test is positive if patient senses that humeral head is about to slip out anteriorly and body stiffens in apprehension. The test is repeated with the anterior part of shoulder protected.

recommended.name: Fulcrum's Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine, arm abducted up to 90 deg. The examiner places their hands over the shoulder to set the fulcrum base. The humeral head is levered forward by extending and externally rotating arm. The patient immediately becomes apprehensive.

recommended.name: Drawer's Test
recommended.procedure: Patient lies supine, scapula is stabilised with one hand while the upper arm is grasped firmly with the other, and manoeuvring is done forward and backward (like a drawer). The drawer's test is positive if instability is marked.

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: Check for periarticular erosions, subchondral sclerosis, and resorption

recommended.name: Radiographic Confirmation
recommended.procedure: Check for distortion of the joint, subchondral sclerosis, osteophyte formation, and narrowing of articular space

recommended.name: Phalen’s Test
recommended.procedure: Patient flexes both wrists maximally (dorsal surfaces pressed together) and holds position for 60 seconds.

recommended.name: Tinel’s Sign
recommended.procedure: Examiner taps lightly over median nerve at volar carpal tunnel using fingertip or reflex hammer.

recommended.name: Carpal Compression Test (Durkan’s Test)
recommended.procedure: Examiner applies direct firm pressure with thumbs over carpal tunnel for up to 30 seconds.

recommended.name: Finkelstein’s Test
recommended.procedure: Patient makes a fist with thumb tucked inside fingers. Examiner gently applies passive ulnar deviation to wrist.

recommended.name: WHAT Test (Wrist Hyperflexion Abduction of Thumb)
recommended.procedure: Patient hyperflexes wrist and actively abducts thumb against examiner resistance.

recommended.name: First Dorsal Compartment Palpation
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates APL and EPB tendons over radial styloid while patient actively moves thumb.

recommended.name: Ligament Stress Tests
recommended.procedure: Examiner applies anteroposterior translation and stress forces to scapholunate, lunotriquetral, and collateral ligaments.

recommended.name: Watson’s Test (Scaphoid Shift Test)
recommended.procedure: Examiner compresses scaphoid tuberosity while moving wrist from ulnar to radial deviation.

recommended.name: TFCC Load Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner places wrist in ulnar deviation, applies axial compressive load, and rotates forearm.

recommended.name: Press Test
recommended.procedure: Patient uses hands to push up and support body weight from a seated position in a chair.

recommended.name: Fovea Sign
recommended.procedure: Examiner presses thumb into soft depression (fovea) between ulnar styloid and flexor carpi ulnaris tendon.

recommended.name: Transillumination Test
recommended.procedure: Light source applied directly against wrist swelling in a darkened room.

recommended.name: Palpation and Fluctuation Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates lump during full wrist flexion and extension.

recommended.name: Resisted Wrist Extension Test
recommended.procedure: Patient extends wrist against examiner resistance with forearm pronated.

recommended.name: Intersection Palpation and Crepitus Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner places fingers over dorsal radial forearm 4-6 cm proximal to wrist while patient flexes and extends wrist.

recommended.name: Snuffbox Tenderness Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates floor of anatomical snuffbox with wrist in slight ulnar deviation.

recommended.name: Scaphoid Compression Test (Axial Thumb Load)
recommended.procedure: Examiner applies axial compressive force through the first metacarpal along axis of thumb into scaphoid.

recommended.name: Scaphoid Tubercle Palpation
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates volar scaphoid tubercle at base of thenar eminence with wrist extended.

recommended.name: Axial Load Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner applies axial compression through wrist and third metacarpal with wrist in neutral.

recommended.name: Lunate Palpation Test
recommended.procedure: Examiner palpates dorsal central wrist directly over lunate fossa in slight flexion.

recommended.name: Radiography and MRI Evaluation
recommended.procedure: Standard PA and lateral wrist radiographs plus MRI if radiographs normal.
